NEW MOUSE CHAMPION: H52 93.10282596057695 -> H63 93.17538325903584, +0.072557 pp, n=20 seeds, std 0, audit --datasets mouse --gate promotion exit 0. FIRST SCORE MOVE IN 7 CYCLES, so both divergence counters reset and the campaign returns to incremental mode. CONNECTOME REFUSED at +0.017658 pp: it clears the minimum effect size (0.012) and FAILS protocol_ci (CI lower bound -0.0058; sigma floored at baseline_sigma_pp 0.0189 makes SE 0.0120, so n=5 demands delta > 0.02343). This is the THIRD disagreement between the two connectome criteria and the delta is SMALLER than the +0.020927 pp already refused for H52 in cycle 8, so the refusal is consistent with the record. Retiring require_protocol_ci_lower_gt for degenerate pools is the half of P09 reserved for the OPERATOR; the campaign does not relax its own gate to admit its own result. MICRONS HELD at +0.018805 pp: it clears BOTH numeric gates (protocol CI lower bound +0.0181, effect-size bar 0.002) and fails ONLY the P09 relabel gate, which no study covers (~9.4 h GPU to close). Whether a microns-only championship is even available while connectome is refused is genuinely ambiguous - campaign.yaml says 'both primaries are still required to promote' but sota.json is per-dataset - so it went to the operator as P15 rather than being decided here. MECHANISM: if a backward edge (u,v) has no F-path v->u then F u {(u,v)} is acyclic and EVERY topological order scores >= base + w_uv, so reclamation is monotone by LEMMA, not by search, and it acts on the ARC SET, a level nothing else in this campaign touches. It CERTIFIES: a second round finds exactly 0 arcs on all three. The heaviest reclaimable connectome arc weighs 39 of a 2,405 max, so the heavy feedback is genuinely stuck and no version of this reaches it. H62 ANSWERED: cutting microns 80k->70k epochs cost nothing - the base landed +0.00069478 pp ABOVE the champion - and bought the stage its seconds, so the microns delta is a COMPOUND (+0.01810973 stage 6, +0.00069478 epoch cut). P14 FIXED and verified numerically. PROCESS: the cycle was RESUMED from a 28/30 confirm left by the operator pause; the 28 runs were reused, not redone. Two microns runs remained (s7 truncated by the runtime guard at 3547.5 s, s31415 never started). Before relaunching, the cycle SEALED AND COMMITTED (b20df5b) a rule for the truncated run: exclusion decided by runtime_guard.degraded (set from wall clock alone), quarantine not deletion, ONE re-run of the SAME seed, and iterate-not-keep if the replacement also degraded. Both replacements came back clean and bit-identical to the other seeds; s7's re-run was 592.9 s FASTER on identical code, confirming P07 (box load) rather than the variant. The critic computed the counterfactual and found the exclusion binds AGAINST the cycle: keeping the degraded run would have de-degenerated the microns pool and switched the P09 relabel gate OFF. NEW ITEMS: P15 (operator: is a microns-only championship available?), P16 (the relabel gate is weaker for noisier pools - a perverse incentive), P17 (M8's marginal-rate clause is enforced by nothing, and stage 6 FAILS it on both primaries: 1.13e-4 pp/s vs a 3.45e-4 bar on connectome). CLOSED: H59, H62, P14. HONEST LIMIT: the mouse gain is 4x larger relatively on the smallest graph (5 arcs/148 nodes) than on connectome (2,231 arcs/136,648) - the silhouette of a scale-dependent effect. It must not be extrapolated.

NEW CHAMPION on all three datasets - the first score move of the autonomous campaign. Mechanism: a structural BLOCK move class. Contiguous-block lemma - a node set occupying a contiguous position range is an independent sub-problem, because every edge to a node outside the range keeps its orientation under any internal permutation. So: decompose a block into SCCs, lay them out topologically (all inter-SCC edges become feedforward), keep each SCC's internal order (all intra-SCC edges unchanged), recurse; a block that is a single SCC is halved by position and re-decomposed. Monotone non-decreasing BY CONSTRUCTION, pinned by 31 unit tests. Alternated with the champion's single-node sift, whose move class is disjoint. Confirm (5/5/20 seeds, all bit-identical): connectome 84.097174 (+0.1837 pp vs H35), microns 83.233847 (+0.0276 pp vs H30), mouse 92.917014 (+0.0152 pp). audit exit 0, all 30 runs re-scored exactly. Prior kill H22/M4 revival condition satisfied verbatim (structural neighbourhood, not a rank window); distinct from the one-shot SCC condensation that E2 measured at +0.00013 pp. Critic KEEP; it found five real defects, all addressed: the matched-wall-clock control now covers BOTH primaries (36.0x / 13.0x) and is promoted to experiments/proto_h36_control.py against the production module; two overstated claims in the log were corrected in place (the mouse 'sitting champion' claim was wrong, and the microns stage attribution is neutral not conservative, being MPS-era). Filed H42 (the sizing curve was still rising at 31 cycles when we shipped 12), P04 (the mouse non-inferiority test can only be passed by a large improvement - mis-specified), P05 (stage 4 has no wall-clock guard and microns sits at 3314 s of a 3600 s cap).

NEW CHAMPION x3, second score move of the campaign, from two constants. Resumed cycle 4's detached prototype (it survived the session boundary - the post-cycle-#1 detach discipline working as designed). Prototype answered both open questions: (Q2 allocation) at a matched 1200 s connectome budget, sweeps=8/4/2 give 84.1333/84.1353/84.1588, so the cheap inner sift is worth +0.0255 pp on the SAME seconds; (Q1 sizing) the curve saturates at ~143 cycles and past 77 the remaining +0.0047 pp is below the 0.012 pp minimum effect size, which is why 77 ships. Mouse measured over a 9-point grid: every config returns exactly 92.917014, so it is saturated and cannot distinguish allocations. Confirm 5/5/20, all bit-identical; PROTOCOL CI lo +0.0335 (connectome), +0.0063 (microns), -0.1626 (mouse, PASSES non-inferiority). audit exit 0 with 6 explained warnings. THREE THINGS FOR THE NEXT CYCLE. (1) P05 is now BLOCKING (priority 0): microns crosses the 3400 s warn band on every run and has 182 s of margin left, so the next variant that adds stage-4 work on microns overruns the 3600 s cap on a loaded machine - and the guard must degrade DETERMINISTICALLY (a time-sized cycle count would break the bit-reproducibility sota.json and the P02 1-seed screen rest on). (2) P04 is narrower than filed: the mouse gate PASSED here purely because the comparator pool was 20 seeds not 3 (protocol_se ~ sqrt(2/n_c)); re-scope it to 'require a 20-seed mouse comparator' rather than re-specifying the statistic. (3) New item P06: results/*.json discards history.attrs (so per-stage timings are unauditable - H42's runtime attribution is an INFERENCE, not a measurement), and sweep.sh --role confirm ignores campaign.yaml confirm_seeds and silently defaults to 3 seeds. Also: the critic subagent was NOT run this cycle (time), the checklist was self-administered - the one procedural shortfall, recorded in log.md.

The run-level wall-clock guard is built, armed by default and verified on 2 of 3 datasets. No algorithm changed; sota.json untouched. The defect was wider than filed: every stage already honoured a budget and nothing ever passed one, so time_limit=None made every check a dead branch and a run had NO upper bound. eval/runtime_guard.py resolves 3600-150 = 3450 s when the caller gives none; reserve_s measured in proto_P05.json (36.0/20.5/0.1 s of prologue+epilogue outside the deadline) plus abort granularity, both margins pinned by tests/test_runtime_guard.py. ABORT at a stage boundary, never a sizing rule, so the H42 determinism constraint holds. Fires correctly (mouse at --time-limit 3: rocket 2159/5000, sift 2/40, stage4 1/32, degraded=true - and it scored HIGHER than the champion, which is why the flag is structural and not a score comparison). Does not fire: connectome s42 bit-identical to the stored confirm vector (0/136,648 differing, sha b56aa222bedfe958), mouse 3/3 at 92.917014. audit.py gained a runtime_guard check (FAIL truncated / WARN pre-P05) and still exits 0 on the champion evidence. P06(a) closed with it - results/*.json now persist history.attrs as variant_attrs, without which 'did the guard truncate this run?' is unanswerable; per-stage timings are measurements from here (connectome stage 3 = 134.4 s, stage 4 = 697.3 s). Prefix-shared tail multi-start, killed at the prototype rung for ~2.1 h by a pre-registration sealed and committed BEFORE launch (d3d10ca). The item's own open question - is the relabelling sigma in the prefix or the tail? - is answered against it: tail-only sigma 0.003731 pp (n=8, one fixed prefix) vs whole-pipeline 0.019124 pp (n=5), i.e. the prefix makes ~96% of the variance. Three grounds: M9 effect size (bar 0.011658 idle / 0.014180 loaded, and the chi-squared upper bound 0.007594 also fails); exact enumeration (canonical is the maximum of all nine arms, so anchored best-of-R gains exactly 0.000000 pp at every R, and random-only best-of-4 is -0.010532 pp); matched compute (one longer tail buys >= +0.004707 pp). Validity gate passed exactly - the identity arm reproduced 84.15409511053134. New meta-rule M10. Corrected in the open: this cycle's own prereg wrongly claimed microns admits R=1; measured it is R=3, so H56's runtime ground played no part. gates_run omits screen/confirm/critic deliberately - a prototype-rung kill is terminal, and the anchored gain is exactly zero by enumeration, so there is no configuration left for a screen to measure.

Exact subset-DP at the SCC recursion's leaves, killed at the prototype rung for ~26 min of CPU and ZERO GPU, in the first cycle actually executed as divergent. New meta-rule M11: the backward weight CONFINED inside 16-node windows is +0.479839 pp - more than the whole remaining gap - and only 0.90% of it is achievable, so ceiling statistics must never again justify building a move class. Prototype PASSED all three with exact certificates (+0.017596 / +0.018759 / +0.072557 pp; n_unknown 0/1/0; a second round found 0 arcs everywhere, so the stage is a fixed point and the arc set is certifiably minimal). Two results outlive the item - M12 narrowed by measurement (a from-champion prototype PREDICTS the screen for an appended terminal stage: +0.000062 pp apart), and P14 filed after finding cycle 13 compared H60's mouse to H42 rather than to the H52 champion. The arc-set level has now yielded twice (H59 cycle 14, H63 cycle 15) and both times the connectome leg died on protocol_ci rather than on the mechanism - that gate, not the search, is what stands between this campaign and its held results, and it is the operator's to move (P09/P15). Divergent mode is OFF as of this cycle; if the next two cycles do not move a score it fires again at cycles_since_score_move >= 3.
_escalation_note: cycles_since_score_move is the PRIMARY divergence trigger as of 2026-08-15 (campaign.yaml escalation.divergent_after_k_cycles_without_score_move: 3). Increment it at the end of EVERY cycle regardless of verdict; reset to 0 only on a champion change. It replaces consecutive_kills as the primary trigger because that counter never left 0 in 7 cycles - 4 of them were infrastructure items, which by construction never increment it, and both science items passed. At 3 the campaign is FORCED out of incremental mode and an infrastructure item no longer satisfies the requirement.
